lines:
Removed the released-payload retention notice from every user-facing surface. Deleted `ReleasedPayloadNotice.tsx` and `releasedPayload.css`, and deleted the presentation helpers in `releasedPayload.ts` (releasedBytesLabel, releasedRequestStatement, releasedSnapshotStatement, releasedPayloadEvidence, releasedPayloadDigest).

Behaviour now: when a payload's heavy bytes were released, the surface shows the omission, not a narrative. ModelCallBlock omits the Input block; ConversationTimeline omits the Input row; ContextUsage omits the breakdown and disables Display Context; ContextPanel renders no body and no longer says "Snapshot released"; runDetails no longer emits a "notice" section and its variant was removed from RunDetailsSection. `releasedPayloadOf`/`releasedModelCallInput`/`releasedContextCheckpoint` are kept, because a surface still needs to detect the tombstone so it never renders a null or an empty document.

Design: `runDetails.ts` is bound to aworkit.desktop_ui.evidence_inspector, but that element's description never described the released-payload notice, so no design text became inaccurate and no design write was needed. The retention policy itself (aworkit.local_store.history_retention) is unchanged.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx vitest run src/chat` -> 283 passed / 3 failed; the 3 are the pre-existing Windows-dialect and cache-unit failures (cacheUsage.test.ts, ToolCallCard.test.tsx, toolCallPresentation.test.ts), already proven pre-existing by running them with the change stashed. The four updated files (releasedPayload, runDetails, ModelCallBlock, ContextUsage) and runtime.integration.test.tsx all pass.

Not verified: the running desktop app has not been rebuilt.

Every older Agent/model-call card now shows the retention "released payload" notice ("Request body released — this turn's snapshot was superseded by newer turns, so its 1.3 MB request body was released to bound this Chat's store size…" plus "Released <time> · 20 newest turns kept"). The user reports this as internal implementation language that must not be user-facing.

Remove the notice from every user-facing surface and leave nothing empty in its place:
- ModelCallBlock (the Agent card) and the generic activity card in ConversationTimeline: omit the Input block when the body was released.
- ContextUsage popover: omit the token breakdown; keep the summary; disable "Display Context" for a released scope with a neutral title.
- ContextPanel: render no body when the scope has no readable document; drop the "Snapshot released" status wording.
- RunDetailsInspector/runDetails: stop emitting the released "notice" section and remove the section variant.
- Delete ReleasedPayloadNotice.tsx and releasedPayload.css, and delete the presentation helpers in releasedPayload.ts (releasedBytesLabel, releasedRequestStatement, releasedSnapshotStatement, releasedPayloadEvidence, releasedPayloadDigest). Keep releasedPayloadOf/releasedModelCallInput/releasedContextCheckpoint, which are still needed to detect a released payload so no surface renders null or an empty document.
- Update releasedPayload.test.ts, ModelCallBlock.test.tsx, ContextUsage.test.tsx and runtime.integration.test.tsx to assert the notice is absent instead of present.

Design: runDetails.ts is bound to aworkit.desktop_ui.evidence_inspector; record the removal there.

data.title: Remove the "released payload" retention notice from the user interface
